_comment: Every rule the team enforces, and WHERE it is enforced. This is the conversion backlog, kept as data so it cannot drift the way prose does: `code` = a command already refuses/does it; `enforcible` = a command could, and the proposal is written down; `judgment` = no mechanism can decide it, a person or model must; `reference` = facts/diagnostics that belong in docs, not in the contract. Print the gap with `devteam docs-audit --rules`. When a rule moves to code, change its kind here and delete the prose that restated it.

rules.rule: never edit project code on main; every task runs on dt/<task-id> cut from origin/main
rules.enforced_by: devteam worktree-start / release

rules.rule: read project code from origin/main, not the checkout
rules.enforced_by: devteam status (DELIVERY line) / storefront-scenes renders from the scan tree

rules.rule: never hand-edit .pipeline/state.json; write via devteam record
rules.proposal: doctor: keep a state checksum written by the CLI and BLOCK when the file changed outside it

rules.rule: .github/workflows/release.yml is generated from team/templates/ci-release.yml
rules.enforced_by: devteam doctor (renders the template and compares the project workflow)

rules.rule: screenshots render from the app's composables; the poster is composed (plate from an image model only), never hand-drawn HTML
rules.enforced_by: devteam storefront-build (refuses without a plate/layout; --builtin must be deliberate) + asset_critic provenance

rules.rule: what the listing says is decided and committed before anything is drawn
rules.enforced_by: devteam storefront-build (refuses without a locked direction) / storefront-direction --apply

rules.rule: the API uploads and commits a listing edit; permissions and Managed publishing are console-only, so the publish is finished in Play Console
rules.note: no mechanism can grant console permissions; the skill states the sequence

rules.rule: every app must have an active launchd nightly schedule (or explicit manual mode in profile.json) verified by doctor and store-readiness
rules.enforced_by: devteam doctor (orchestrator check) + devteam store-readiness (Automation & Operations category)

rules.rule: a screen whose look/feel fingerprint changed must get one neutral first-use reaction before a run can claim it polished anything; unchanged screens are never re-audited
rules.enforced_by: devteam ux-plan / ux-audit (fingerprint decides) + team/verify.py warn naming the unaudited screens
rules.note: warning, not a gate: the released gates stay compile/tests. Per-screen fingerprints mean the audit is paid on change, never per release

rules.rule: a GA4 connection is ready only when the declared property can actually be read; the credential is a reader service account (connections.ga4.key_file or machine-wide $DEVTEAM_GA4_KEY), never the owner's ADC login — Google blocks analytics.readonly for gcloud's default client
rules.enforced_by: team/ga4.py (one credential resolver + a real runReport probe) used by team/research.py and devteam doctor
rules.note: lesson 2026-11-05: doctor tested 'gcloud can mint a token', so a property returning 403 (and a login Google had just blocked) still read as configured; a new project now cannot land there either

rules.rule: every scheduled app runs RUNS_PER_DAY (3) times a night inside the owner's 23:00–11:00 window; apps are interleaved evenly so consecutive machine-wide runs are as far apart as the app count allows, and overlap is tolerated because three runs make a skipped one harmless
rules.enforced_by: devteam setup (scheduler.plan_schedule/apply_plan installs 3 slots per app) + devteam schedules --rebalance (re-spaces every app) + devteam doctor and store-readiness (assert 3 slots inside the window)
rules.note: owner directive 2026-11-05: three runs a night, 11pm–11am, overlap tolerated but avoided where possible; MIN_GAP_MIN is now a best-effort target, not a refusal

rules.rule: pick and record prune; a tree goes only when its work is safe somewhere else
rules.enforced_by: devteam worktree-prune (dry run by default) / pick / record

rules.rule: work is closed when main contains it or origin holds its branch; unfinished work is parked
rules.enforced_by: worktrees.park + devteam takeover (parked list)

rules.rule: no frozen paths, release-knob diff or dependency gates; compile/tests are the gates — and a production change must carry its own test in the same diff
rules.enforced_by: devteam verify (diff-scoped test gate) / devteam release (same gate before the bump)

rules.rule: every changed production file is named by a test file in the same diff; a changed UI file is named by a Compose/Espresso test with an assertion, never a screenshot render
rules.enforced_by: devteam verify (test gate) / devteam release (refuses before the version bump) / devteam doctor (test-posture warn)

rules.rule: 100% unit and UI test coverage is enforced by code; when below 100%, the planner must make raising coverage the topmost priority (queue HEAD)
rules.enforced_by: config/coverage.json / team/coverage.py (100% floors) / team/research.py (_validate rejects non-test queue HEAD) / devteam doctor (coverage WARN)

rules.rule: ask the owner only for what no agent can decide (incidents, WIP, direction); never about promotion
rules.note: requires intent; the run banner is where it shows

rules.rule: every change ends in a commit on a pushed ref; a dirty checkout is reported
rules.note: warn-only by design: the run commits its own work, it does not commit the owner's
rules.enforced_by: devteam doctor / status (checkout_dirty — reports, never commits the owner's WIP)

rules.rule: never push with red gates
rules.enforced_by: devteam release (refuses on FAIL) / verify

rules.rule: a whatsnew_curated project never gets the pipeline's boilerplate note, but an explicit per-release `whatsnew` in the task spec IS written; no release may repeat the previous release's note verbatim
rules.enforced_by: shipper.whatsnew_gate (verify + release refuse a repeated/empty note) / store-readiness

rules.rule: a run stops only the emulators it started
rules.enforced_by: devteam emulators --record / verify (baseline diff)

rules.rule: three emulator-only failure modes (corrupt snapshot, AVD lock, crash-consent dialog) and how to repair them
rules.note: diagnostics, not a rule: 20 lines of troubleshooting sitting in the contract

rules.rule: a surprise is closed by a change to team code in the same run; nothing is appended to a log
rules.note: no mechanism can decide what surprised an agent, but the FIX must be a commit; a fix too large for the run becomes an `enforcible` entry here

rules.rule: team code carries no project names
rules.enforced_by: devteam doctor (greps every registered project name)

rules.rule: the newest text is the source of truth; overlapping copies are removed, not kept
rules.enforced_by: devteam docs-audit --check --new-only (pre-commit hook)

rules.rule: a run's starting position (delivery ref, dirty files, trees, queue head, open asks, next command) is read, not inferred from prose
rules.enforced_by: devteam takeover

rules.rule: a device gate that cannot boot because a dead emulator still holds the AVD must repair the AVD and rerun, never silently degrade to warn-only
rules.proposal: devteam verify's instrumented stage: before booting an AVD, if a qemu process holds that AVD's lock while `adb devices` shows no online device AND this run started no emulator, terminate the holder, clear the locks, boot again, and only then fall back to warn-only; record the repair in the run log
rules.note: 2026-11-05/06: the two touched device classes passed (13 tests), then a zombie qemu from a failed boot kept the AVD lock, every later boot died in ~1s, and verify degraded to 'device test runner could not execute (warn-only)' — the degrade is right for a machine with no emulator, wrong for a repairable lock holder

rules.rule: the plan has a middle tier: vision → goals (the ENDS, one number each) → milestones (the MEANS) → tasks; a new milestone must sit under a goal, and a later goal's milestones are not planned while an earlier goal's number fails
rules.enforced_by: team/goals.py (ensure_goal_tier, tree_gaps, validate_advances) — devteam adapt re-shapes the tree, devteam doctor gates it, the planner's goal gate refuses the queue

rules.rule: a listing frame must be painted from a render that contains the screen it depicts; a poster older than the newest change to its scene's composables is stale, not current
rules.proposal: store-readiness/store-publish compare the source commit recorded for the painted frames (.pipeline/storefront_run.json + docs/storefront-frames.json composition) with the newest commit that touched each scene's bound composables in docs/storefront.json: a frame whose scene changed after the paint is reported as STALE and store-publish refuses it until `devteam storefront-build <project> --poster` repaints it.
rules.note: run-derived 2026-11-06 (Paddle v1.0.40): verify warned 'History changed (render), no audit since' while the listing's 03_summary/04_history posters still depicted the previous build, and every readiness check passed 25/25 because nothing compares the frames' source commit with the shipped screens.

rules.rule: the installed launcher must be provably the same design as the Play listing icon; a warning that no check can ever clear is a defect in the check, not a finding about the app
rules.proposal: store-readiness 'Installed Icon Matches Store Listing': when the app ships an adaptive VECTOR launcher (mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml) and no PNG mipmap, render the vector's foreground+background pair at 512x512 (or compare the listing icon against the adaptive icon's declared colors) and report parity from that render instead of the current 'no launcher bitmap to compare' WARNING, which no adaptive-icon project can ever clear
rules.note: run-derived 2026-11-07 (BookSwapKMP v1.0.2): every store-readiness run carried this WARNING while the listing icon (Stitch) and the adaptive launcher are the only icon assets the project ships; the same run also found the keystore check passing the scan tree instead of the project, so a real backup read as missing

rules.rule: competitor research may not present a figure it did not read: no default rating (the parser fills 4.5 when the listing gave none), no 'not stated' rendered as a value, and no search-answer fragment presented as a listing feature
rules.why: 2026-11-08: `devteam competition` produced a gate-passing document that listed the project itself as its own rival, a cybersecurity MDR portal as a field-inspection benchmark, and 4.5★ for every app (a parser default, not a reading). The store blocker would have been 'cleared' by data the owner could not trust; the document was not committed.
rules.proposal: `_parse_recon_search_output` carries rating=None (never 4.5) when the listing gave none; `devteam store-readiness` refuses docs/COMPETITION_RESEARCH.md that renders a 'not stated' rating/install as a value, or a feature bullet containing 'the sources do not provide' / 'no specific mention'
rules.note: 2026-11-08: `devteam competition` produced a gate-passing document that listed the project itself as its own rival, a cybersecurity MDR portal as a field-inspection benchmark, and 4.5 stars for every app (a parser default, not a reading). The document was not committed; self-exclusion and the search-term fallback are already fixed in code.

rules.rule: a milestone measure that names a server-side effect ('RPC succeeds', 'scan is sent', 'handshake completes') is only marked met with a recorded live probe; reading the call site and passing fake-transport tests is not evidence that the call lands
rules.proposal: a measure may carry {"probe": "<command>"}; devteam plan --apply-result runs it (or refuses the verdict when the measure text names a backend path and no probe exists), exactly as metric measures are already evaluated by code. Today the orchestrator's 'cheap check' is prose.
rules.note: run-derived 2026-11-08 (BookSwapKMP v1.0.3): m1 'Local Supabase RPC book requests succeed' was retired as met because BookSwapRepository forwarded requestBook/verifyHandoff to the RPCs and tests passed on a fake transport — the app actually boots to Discovery with no sign-in (App.kt default destination, in-memory SessionStore), so the RPCs post with the anon key and auth.uid() is NULL. The owner found it by hand; the gates could not, because the defect is 'the default entry never authenticates', which no diff-scoped test names.

rules.rule: ux-audit, ux-video and ux-flow judge a DEVICE (emulator or connected phone) — never an off-device render; integration tests run OFF a device (JVM/Robolectric) and verify never boots one for them
rules.enforced_by: team/emulator.require_device() is the only way the three UX passes get a serial (it raises when none is available); team/verify.device_gate runs verify.integration_task on the JVM or skips, and no longer boots an AVD
rules.note: owner policy 2026-11-08. run-derived: ux-audit used to judge a Robolectric render, which cannot show a keyboard covering the submit button, an inset collision, a session that failed to persist, or an unreachable network — all found within an hour of moving the audit onto the device.
